title: Present simple, present continuous, stative verbs
subtitle: Habits, actions in progress, and verbs that describe states

rows.example: Lina **goes** to swimming practice every Tuesday.
I **like** the new detective series on TV.

blocks.intro: The present simple often appears with these adverbs and time phrases:
items: phrases: {pill:every Monday} {pill:each week} {pill:once a week} {pill:three times a month}
These adverbs usually go **before** the main verb, but **after** the verb **be**.
I **am** {pill:often} late for my piano lessons.

blocks.text: The verbs **be** and **have** use irregular present forms.
blocks.note: See the irregular verb list at the back of your notes.

rows.example: She **is working** at the museum until the end of the month.
My brother **is always borrowing** my headphones without asking!

blocks.intro: The present continuous often appears with these words and phrases:

blocks.text: Stative verbs do not usually describe actions. They describe states (feelings, thoughts, possession, senses). They are not normally used in continuous tenses.

blocks.correct: I **like** reading books in my free time.
blocks.incorrect: I **am liking** reading books in my free time.

blocks.text: Some of these verbs (such as **be**, **have** and **think**) are used in continuous tenses when they describe **actions**.
blocks.note: **What do you think** about his new song? (opinion) · **I'm thinking** about last night's match. (mental process)

exercises.title: A · Write a sentence
exercises.instruction: Use the prompts to write a full sentence. Choose present simple or present continuous.

items.prompt: Lina / take / the train / every morning
acceptedAnswers: Lina takes the train every morning.
Lina takes the train every morning

items.prompt: the children / play / in the garden / right now
acceptedAnswers: The children are playing in the garden right now.
The children are playing in the garden right now
The children are playing in the garden at the moment.

items.prompt: Omar / not / like / spicy food
acceptedAnswers: Omar does not like spicy food.
Omar does not like spicy food

items.prompt: you / wait / for the bus / at the moment?
acceptedAnswers: Are you waiting for the bus at the moment?
Are you waiting for the bus at the moment

items.prompt: we / usually / have / lunch at one
acceptedAnswers: We usually have lunch at one.
We usually have lunch at one

items.prompt: she / always / lose / her keys! (annoying habit)
acceptedAnswers: She is always losing her keys!
She is always losing her keys.
items.explanation: Use present continuous + always for an annoying repeated action.

exercises.title: B · Complete the sentences
exercises.instruction: Write the correct present simple or present continuous form in each gap.

items.prompt: Maya ___ at the library on Saturdays. (work)
Listen! The neighbours ___ again. (argue)
I ___ this map. (not / understand)
items.explanation: Understand is stative here, so use the present simple.

items.prompt: Right now the museum ___ a free evening tour. (offer)
They ___ with us until Friday. (stay)
Water ___ at 100°C. (boil)

exercises.title: C · Rewrite the sentence
exercises.instruction: Rewrite each sentence so the verb in bold uses the tense suggested in brackets.

items.prompt: This week Maya **stays** with her aunt in Leeds. (temporary)
acceptedAnswers: This week Maya is staying with her aunt in Leeds.
This week Maya is staying with her aunt in Leeds
Maya is staying with her aunt in Leeds this week.
Maya is staying with her aunt in Leeds this week

items.prompt: I **think** about last night's puzzle. (mental process now)
acceptedAnswers: I'm thinking about last night's puzzle.
I'm thinking about last night's puzzle
I am thinking about last night's puzzle.
I am thinking about last night's puzzle

items.prompt: They **have** lunch in the garden at the moment. (action)
acceptedAnswers: They're having lunch in the garden at the moment.
They're having lunch in the garden at the moment
They are having lunch in the garden at the moment.
They are having lunch in the garden at the moment

items.prompt: She **always complains** about the noise. (annoying habit)
acceptedAnswers: She's always complaining about the noise.
She's always complaining about the noise
She is always complaining about the noise.
She is always complaining about the noise

exercises.title: D · Choose the correct option
exercises.instruction: Select the phrase that completes each sentence.

items.prompt: I ___ her from school — we were in the same class.
We ___ at a hotel this week while the kitchen is painted.
He ___ his mug in the sink!
Ice ___ at 0°C.
What ___ of this plan? I need your opinion.
Quiet, please — I ___ to the podcast.

exercises.title: E · Word bank
exercises.instruction: Complete each sentence with a phrase from the word bank. You will not need every form twice.

items.prompt: This soup ___ delicious.
The chef ___ the soup now.
We ___ a great time at the festival.
They ___ two cats and a rabbit.
I ___ that story for a second.
She ___ at the photos on the wall.

exercises.title: F · Find and correct the mistakes
exercises.instruction: Tap the verb that is wrong, then write the correct form.
exercises.paragraph: Every morning I {click:am getting} up at six. Right now I {click:write} this email on the train. I {click:am knowing} most of the people in my office. This week we {click:work} from a studio by the river. My colleague {click:always is interrupting} me when I try to focus.

items.explanation: A regular habit uses the present simple.
